description.summary: arrange a claim's own surfaces inside its region

protocol.description:
A screen has two owners. The Layout that a Display names owns the screen: display-operator gives each claim a region of it, and no workload can move a region. Inside its region, a claim's surfaces belong to one arranger: the first client of the claim that asks for this protocol. The arranger states where each of the claim's surfaces shows, how opaque it is, and in what order they stack, and the compositor tweens every surface from where it shows to where the arrangement puts it, on each repaint of the output. A video player can so be made of several surfaces, from several programs, and move between arrangements with one request.
liken-layout.so, the compositor module that display-operator ships, offers this protocol. Only a client that arrived on a claim's socket may arrange, and an arrangement acts only on surfaces of that claim. It never moves a surface outside the region, and never scales one above the region's size. The arranger's own surfaces are surfaces of the claim like any other, and an arrangement may place them.

interface.name: liken_arranger_manager_v1

description.summary: hands out the arranger of a claim

interface.description: The global. The compositor advertises it on every socket. A client that did not arrive on a claim's socket gets an arranger that sends refused.

request.name: destroy
request.description: An arranger that the manager created stays.

request.name: get_arranger

description.summary: ask to arrange the caller's claim

request.description: Creates an arranger object. The compositor answers with granted when the claim has no arranger, and with refused when it has one or when the caller is on no claim.

interface.name: liken_arranger_v1

description.summary: the one client that arranges a claim's region

interface.description:
An arrangement is a list of entries, built with entry and applied with commit. Each entry names the surfaces of the claim whose xdg app_id matches, and states their rectangle, opacity, fit, and delay. The order of the entries is the stacking order, first at the bottom. A surface that no entry names keeps the default: it fills the region, shows fully opaque, and stacks below every named surface in the order the surfaces arrived. Before the first commit, every surface has the default, and the claim's surfaces keep the stacking order that the operator gave them. An arrangement with no entries keeps that order too.
A rectangle is in logical pixels of the region, with the region's top-left corner at 0,0. The region event states its size.
When the arranger is destroyed, or its client disconnects, every surface of the claim tweens back to the default over 400 milliseconds, and the claim has no arranger until a client asks again.

entry.name: invalid_rect
entry.summary: the rectangle is empty or reaches outside the region

entry.name: invalid_opacity
entry.summary: the opacity is below 0 or above 1

entry.name: invalid_duration
entry.summary: a duration or delay is above 10000 milliseconds

entry.name: duplicate_entry
entry.summary: two entries of one arrangement name the same app_id

entry.name: not_granted
entry.summary: an entry or commit before granted, or after refused

entry.name: invalid_enum
entry.summary: a fit or a curve that the enum does not name

entry.name: not_a_claim
entry.summary: the client did not arrive on a claim's socket

entry.name: scale

description.summary: scale the surface, never resize it

entry.description: The compositor scales the surface's content into the rectangle and never sends its client a configure. This fits video, whose client should not reallocate while it plays. When the surface's own content is a single solid colour and it has subsurfaces, as a video player's backdrop does, the surface keeps filling the region at its stacking position and the rectangle applies to its subsurfaces.

entry.name: resize

description.summary: scale during the tween, then resize

entry.description: The compositor scales the surface during the tween, then sends its client one configure at the rectangle's size when the entry lands, and stops scaling when the client commits a buffer of that size. This fits a panel of text, which should redraw at its new size to stay sharp.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Every surface of the claim tweens back to the default.

request.name: entry

description.summary: add one entry to the pending arrangement

request.description: Entries accumulate until commit. The surfaces that app_id names begin their tween delay_ms milliseconds after the commit and end it with the arrangement's duration after that, so an arrangement can stagger its entries.

request.name: commit
request.description: The pending entries become the arrangement, and the pending list is emptied. Every surface of the claim tweens from where it shows now, including a surface partway through an earlier tween, to where the new arrangement puts it. A duration of zero moves them at once. The compositor reports name to display-operator, which shows it in the Display's status. serial comes back in landed.

event.name: refused
event.description: Sent once, right after get_arranger, in place of granted.

event.name: granted
event.description: Sent once, right after get_arranger. A region event follows.

event.name: region

description.summary: the size of the claim's region

event.description: Sent after granted, and again whenever the operator places the region at another size. The size is 0 by 0 while the operator has placed no surface of the claim, and the compositor then checks no rectangle against it. The arrangement keeps its pixel rectangles, so the arranger commits again when the size matters to it.

event.name: surfaces

description.summary: how many surfaces of the claim have an app_id

event.description: Sent after granted for every app_id the claim's surfaces carry, and again whenever that count changes. A count of zero means the last surface with that app_id is gone.

event.name: landed
event.description: Every entry of the commit with this serial finished its tween in the frame the compositor just posted. A commit that a later commit replaced sends no landed.
